assistant|refinery_process_list_caveat: The listed processes are only some of those at each refinery; specific processes vary depending on crude oil type processed and market demand for petroleum products
assistant|atmospheric_distillation_descr: Atmospheric distillation is the first step in refining, where crude oil is heated and separated into different fractions based on boiling points
assistant|fluid_catalytic_cracking_descr: Fluid catalytic cracking (FCC) breaks down heavier fractions of crude oil into lighter, more valuable products such as gasoline and diesel fuel
assistant|alkylation_description: Alkylation combines smaller molecules to form larger ones, creating high-octane gasoline components
assistant|hydrotreating_description: Hydrotreating removes sulfur and other impurities from gasoline and diesel fractions to improve their quality
assistant|delayed_coking_description: Delayed coking breaks down heavy, residual oils into lighter products such as naphtha, diesel, and petroleum coke
assistant|hydrocracking_description: Hydrocracking uses hydrogen and a catalyst to break down heavier fractions of crude oil into lighter, more valuable products
